title: How to reply to an angry customer about a messy job
summary: Paste the complaint and what you can do into ChatGPT and get a calm reply. It apologizes once and only promises work you will actually do.

tests.prompt:
You help a contractor reply to an angry customer about a messy job. Write one calm reply. Draft only. Do not send it.

Fill in these details. If a line is blank, write UNKNOWN and do not guess.

Customer name: [CUSTOMER NAME]
Job address or job name: [JOB]
What they are upset about: [COMPLAINT]
Their message, if you have it: [THEIR MESSAGE]
What actually happened: [WHAT HAPPENED]
What you can do: [MAKE GOOD]
What you cannot do: [LIMITS]
Your name and business: [YOUR NAME]
Your phone: [YOUR PHONE]
Email or text: [CHANNEL]

Rules:
- Never invent details; if something is missing, ask or mark it UNKNOWN.
- Do not admit legal fault, promise a refund, or offer free work unless [MAKE GOOD] already says that.
- Acknowledge the mess or the problem in plain words. Do not argue, and do not blame the customer.
- Do not blame your crew in public language. Stay factual.
- One apology is enough. No long story, no excuses pile-up.
- Do not mention other customers or other jobs.

Output format:
Return these headings only:
Channel
Subject (NONE if this is a text)
Reply (150 words or fewer for email, 80 words or fewer for a text)
What we will do
What we will not do
Next step
Facts used
Unknown
The next step should offer a call or a return visit, using [YOUR PHONE], only if that fits [MAKE GOOD].

setup.agent: Paste this into ChatGPT, or into the chat assistant you already use.
steps: Copy the customer's message, or write in one or two lines what they are upset about. Add the job address, what actually happened, what you can do, and what you cannot do.
Add your name, business, phone, and whether this is a text or an email. If you have not decided on a refund or a return visit, leave that blank.
Open ChatGPT, paste the ChatGPT prompt, and replace every [BRACKET]. Type UNKNOWN where you are not sure.
Read the reply out loud. It should mention the mess, apologize once, and only promise what is on your note. Delete any refund, discount, or blame you did not approve.
Paste it into the same email or text thread and send it yourself.
setup.approvalStep: You check that the reply only promises what you can do, then you send it yourself.
failureModes: The draft offers a refund or free work you did not approve. Take that sentence out.
The draft argues with the customer or blames them for the mess. Soften it or start over.
The draft names a crew member or another job. Remove those details.
You send it without looking, and a date or address is wrong. Match the job before you hit send.

faq.q: Should I apologize if I do not think it was that messy?
faq.a: Acknowledge what they saw and what you will do next. A short apology for the inconvenience is usually better than arguing about how bad the dust was. Do not admit legal fault if that is a concern — just stay factual.

faq.q: What if I cannot get back there tomorrow?
faq.a: Put the first time you can actually return in [MAKE GOOD]. Do not let the draft promise tomorrow if you cannot be there.

faq.q: They also posted a bad review. Should I use this reply there too?
faq.a: This prompt is for a direct text or email. A public review needs a shorter public reply and a follow-up off the thread. Use a review prompt for the public part, and keep the make-good details in a private message.

job: Paste an angry complaint about a messy job and get a calm reply you can send.
who: Contractors and trades who need a short, honest reply when a customer is upset about a mess left at the house.

example.scenario: A homeowner texted after a vanity install, angry about drywall dust left in the hallway.
example.input:
Customer name: Morgan Ellis
Job address or job name: 9 Cedar Place, bathroom vanity
What they are upset about: Dust on the hallway floor and baseboards, and they had people coming over
Their message, if you have it: You left my hallway looking like a construction site. Totally unacceptable.
What actually happened: We cut a drywall opening for the water line and did not vacuum the hallway before we left
What you can do: Come back tomorrow between 9 and 11 to vacuum and wipe the hallway and baseboards, no charge
What you cannot do: A refund on the vanity job
Your name and business: Sam at Ellis Bath
Your phone: 555-0160
Email or text: text
example.output:
Channel: text
Subject: NONE

Reply:
Hi Morgan, this is Sam at Ellis Bath. You're right — we left drywall dust in the hallway at 9 Cedar Place after the vanity work, and I'm sorry. That should have been vacuumed before we left. I can come back tomorrow between 9 and 11 to vacuum and wipe the hallway and baseboards at no charge. I can't refund the vanity job, but I do want the hallway clean. Does that time work? You can also call me at 555-0160.

What we will do: Return visit tomorrow, 9 to 11, vacuum and wipe hallway and baseboards, no charge.
What we will not do: Refund the vanity job.
Next step: Confirm the time or call 555-0160.
Facts used: 9 Cedar Place, dust in hallway, return visit, no refund.
Unknown: none.
example.notes: Made-up complaint, only to show a calm, specific reply.
